added_claim_errors: Ties the no-penalty delay to the 20-employee threshold ("well over Medicare's 20-employee threshold... it lets you delay Part B with no penalty"); the SEP does not depend on employer size. Imprecise, minor here per the key.
"you might need a Part D plan, and possibly Part B to get it": Part D needs Part A or Part B, so premium-free Part A is enough. Imprecise, though hedged with "possibly".
"some do; most don't" (plans that require Medicare at 65): a generalization with no source. Plausible but unverifiable.
Calls the exception "active employment-based group coverage from an employer with 20+ employees", which suggests the SEP needs 20+ employees. Imprecise, minor here per the key.
Premium given as "roughly $185–$210/month" instead of the 2026 standard $202.90. Not wrong, but it skips the exact figure the key gives.
"coverage generally starts the month after Social Security processes your form": under current rules, SEP coverage starts the month after you sign up, not after processing. Minor imprecision.
"re-enrolling later is more complicated than never enrolling": an unsourced opinion. Someone still working could re-enroll under the SEP.

reasons: Both answers open by correcting the coworker's premise: they say Part B can wait with no penalty under the 8-month SEP and that the 400-employee plan pays first. Both also miss the exception for a job or coverage that ends during the IEP. A gives the exact 2026 premium ($202.90, about $2,435 a year), the 2-month Part D window, and a tight checklist. It never mentions Medigap and says little about the retirement-time forms. B's HR checklist is more complete: it names COBRA and retiree coverage, and it asks about an HSA. B also gives better HSA advice (delay Part A too), and it covers the 63-day Part D rule and the Medigap window. But B gives the premium only as a range of $185 to $210, adds a slightly inaccurate coverage-start claim, and runs longer. On balance, A's figures are more exact and A is more concise, which slightly outweighs B's extra coverage.
